method: Editorial reading of the listed primary documentation for these specific claims. HTTP availability is recorded separately. No ASR or exhaustive course validation is implied.

claims.claim: The standard guide lists five domains and 19 objectives; standard weights remain 22/25/20/15/18.
claims.note: Guide v4.2 PDF and the certification page re-read on 2026-11-08. Section titles, objective titles 1.1 to 5.5 and the weights (about 22, 25, 20, 15 and 18 percent) match the site. The guide is not in the Google Developer Knowledge MCP corpus, so it was checked directly. Independent coverage labels are not a guarantee of exam readiness.

claims.claim: Managed Kafka provisions brokers from configured resources; topic retention remains a workload decision.
claims.note: No fixed limits, throughput promises or pricing amounts were copied.

claims.claim: Serverless Spark supports batch workloads and interactive sessions without a user-provisioned cluster.
claims.note: Cluster-specific dependency compatibility must still be tested.

claims.claim: Dataflow streaming defaults to exactly-once mode and supports at-least-once mode; distinct business publications need a stable identity.
claims.note: External side effects and sink write guarantees are separate.

claims.claim: External BigLake object access is delegated and read-only in BigQuery; managed Iceberg has documented mutations.
claims.note: No claim of universal external-writer support.

claims.claim: LIMIT on non-clustered BigQuery tables does not lower bytes read; dry runs and maximum bytes billed serve different guardrail roles.
claims.note: Estimates have limitations; local scan models do not predict actual invoices.

claims.claim: REQUIRED to NULLABLE is relaxation; making an existing NULLABLE field REQUIRED requires recreation.
claims.note: Verify exact table and ingestion method before implementation.

claims.claim: Managed Airflow coordinates DAG tasks; repeatable tasks should pin input intervals and use safe retry behavior.
claims.note: Current managed product names are shown alongside exam-guide terminology.

claims.claim: Storage Transfer Service handles supported file/object paths; Transfer Appliance provides physical shipment; cp supports ad hoc copies.
claims.note: Source support, logistics and reconciliation are part of the decision.

claims.claim: Operational engines and analytical stores have different transaction and access contracts.
claims.note: No blanket latency, availability, price or compatibility promise.

claims.claim: Dataflow system latency, freshness and backlog differ from Pub/Sub subscription backlog age.
claims.note: Metric visibility and gaps do not prove complete business data.

claims.claim: Beam collections and transforms distinguish bounded input, event-time grouping and result emission.
claims.note: Runner behavior and sink corrections still require tests.

claims.claim: Cloud Storage classes, lifecycle automation and retention protection answer different requirements.
claims.note: File-size and compaction suggestions are original workload hypotheses, without universal thresholds.

claims.claim: Workload identity permissions, delegated table access and metadata discovery are distinct boundaries.
claims.note: A network boundary or catalog entry is not a data permission.
